summary: Aermotor steel tower in Bedford County, Virginia; originally Virginia Department of Forestry, now private. Registered 2014; the register and a 1964 survey disagree on height.

facts.design: Aermotor four-legged steel tower with glass cab

access.note: The Register says the tower is now privately owned.

events.note: Coast and Geodetic Survey station description: four-legged steel tower with glass cab, painted gray, overall height 100 feet. The register gives 80 feet.

evidence.supports: 80-foot Aermotor steel tower in Bedford County
evidence.quote: Bedford Fire Tower is an 80-foot Aermotor steel tower located in Bedford County, Virginia.

evidence.supports: landmark for travelers on US 460 between Roanoke and Bedford
evidence.quote: It serves as a prominent landmark for many miles for travelers on US Route 460 between Roanoke and Bedford.
Originally owned by the Virginia Department of Forestry, Bedford tower is now privately owned.

corrections.proposed: Private owner (originally Virginia Department of Forestry)
corrections.why: The register says the tower was originally owned by the Virginia Department of Forestry and is now privately owned; the agency field presents VDOF as the current administrator.

notes_for_editor: No build date in any page read. Height conflict unresolved: the register and the Forest Lookouts header say 80 ft (record height_m 24.4); the 1964 survey description says 100 ft. Ownership change date not found. The Forest Lookouts page also gives driving directions to the tower through a gate and along a private road; they are deliberately left out of the story, which says the tower is private. Do not confuse with Apple Orchard Mountain (Bedford County, listed gone). No staffing or fire history found. Present condition not verified. The Bedford city history page that a search returned covers fire departments, not this tower, and was not used.
